messages:
alex: Heads-up — ran a controlled perf experiment for the KV cache: weighted-evict + periodic compaction + aggressive slot-aging. I ran 2h traces against prod-ish traffic sample and collected pprof + runtime counters. Results are mixed.

tara: Awesome, can you paste the top-level numbers? hitrate / tail latency / OOMs? :eyes: 

alex: Quick summary: hit-rate went from 62% -> 69% (good), median token latency +0.7ms, p95 +2.9ms, and we saw two OOM-ish spikes on node-group-3 during compaction windows.

sasha: Two OOM spikes... were those GPU or CPU mem OOMs? Could be fragmentation during compaction.

alex: GPU-side. The compaction pass attempts to coalesce free segments, but the kernel-selection jitter for short sequences caused KV allocations to be temporarily larger (new kernel path allocates additional buffers), which pushes a few pods over the threshold.

viktor: Did you correlate with batching profile? If batching heuristics changed, we might be switching kernels more often, which can increase peak memory.

alex: Yup — here is the short profiling excerpt (pprof flame sample + allocator stats):

```
pprof: top 10
  31.2%  runtime.gpu_alloc
  18.7%  kernel_picker:pick_kernel_for_seq_len
  14.5%  kv_cache.compact_pass
  10.1%  batch_scheduler:flush
  7.3%   allocator.free_coalesce
  ...

allocator stats (snapshot):
  total_gpu_allocated: 62.1GB
  total_free_fragments: 423
  avg_fragment_size: 120KB
  largest_free_block: 3.2GB
  compaction_rounds: 18
  compaction_success_coalesce: 9
  compaction_aborts_due_to_kernel: 2
```

alex: Notice compaction_success_coalesce ~= 50% and compaction_aborts_due_to_kernel > 0 — those aborts align with the OOM spikes.

tara: Interesting. So compaction is beneficial for steady-state hit-rate but unsafe during short bursts. Can we gate compaction behind a low-load signal or do it on a different time-slice?

sasha: Another angle: reduce kernel selection variance by normalizing sequence length buckets. If kernel_picker is oscillating between small/large kernels, we can bias toward the smaller-kernel path for KV compaction windows. That reduces ephemeral peak.

viktor: We should also consider a weighted eviction scoring that favors consolidating adjacent slots (spatial locality) instead of purely LRU timestamp. That would increase coalescing probability during compaction.

alex: I prototyped an "adjacent-weight" where an entry gets +0.4 score if neighboring slot free. With that change, compaction_success_coalesce went to 78% in a 30m replay and no OOMs. Hit-rate stayed ~68%. BUT we saw slight p95 regression (about +1.1ms) because eviction now sometimes picks slightly hotter keys.

tara: Trade-off matrix then: better fragmentation, better p95 vs slightly worse tail. Do we have SLA headroom to accept +1.1ms p95? Ops? @infra-bot any automated alert thresholds triggered during the experiment?

infra-bot: deploy-telemetry: no customer-facing SLA alerts triggered. internal latency budget flag was crossed for 3 minutes during the earlier run (pre-adjacent-weight).

alex: Proposed mitigations: 1) disable synchronous compaction during burst windows (detect by kernel-picker churn or batch queue length), 2) enable adjacent-weighted eviction by default behind a kill-switch, 3) tweak kernel-picker to prefer smaller-kernel path when compaction-scan is pending.

sasha: Also add a short jitter to compaction start to avoid herd compaction across pods. 50-200ms randomized start per pod.

viktor: For monitoring, add a compact_pass.aborts counter + a compaction_peak_mem gauge and an allocator.fragmentation_ratio = total_free_fragments * avg_fragment_size / total_gpu_allocated. Useful for alerting before OOM.

tara: SGTM. Can we run a 12h soak w/adjacent-weight + kernel preference + jitter? I'll schedule on canary fleet tomorrow. Also add a policy: if compaction_aborts_due_to_kernel > 0 then immediately backoff compaction for 60s.

alex: I'll push the feature flags and metrics today. Will attach the replay script + raw trace to the issue. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sasha: nice work. If soak looks clean we can roll to 50% and keep tracing on.

viktor: One last note — update docs for cache keying: when we favor adjacent-weight we must ensure key hashing preserves locality (slot assignment change could reduce benefit). I'll open a small PR to the key-hash shim to document the trade-offs.

alex: Filed the follow-ups. Closing this thread once the canary is green.
